memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'I will send an angel before you and drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. Go up to the land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people and I might destroy you on the way.'" - Exod 33:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read God's offer carefully. Protection — yes. Victory over enemies — yes. A rich and fertile land — yes. Everything Israel had been travelling toward.

Everything except Himself.

This is one of the most searching moments in the Old Testament, because it exposes what we actually want. Would we be satisfied with God's gifts if God Himself were absent? Many of us would. We would take the land, the security, the good outcome, and never notice the silence.

God's stated reason is mercy, not cruelty. His holiness among a stubborn people would be dangerous to them — "I might destroy you on the way." A holy God dwelling in the middle of unrepentant sin is not a comfortable arrangement.

But this reveals the deepest problem the Bible sets out to solve: how can a holy God live among sinful people without consuming them? Sinai could not answer it. The tabernacle only pictured it. The answer finally came with a name — Immanuel, God with us (Matt 1:23). At the cross, the holiness that would have destroyed us fell on Christ, so that God could dwell in us by His Spirit (1 Cor 6:19).

Do not settle for the land without the Lord.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Would you be content with God's blessings if God Himself felt absent?
2. What "milk and honey" are you chasing right now?
3. How does Christ make God's presence with you possible?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I do not want Your gifts more than I want You. Be with me — that is my greatest treasure. Amen.
